title: Sports Stars of Kazakhstan
paragraphs: Kazakhstan has produced many world-class athletes. From boxing to cycling, from weightlifting to wrestling, Kazakh sportspeople have won medals at the Olympics, World Championships, and Asian Games.

One of the most celebrated is Gennady Golovkin, known as 'GGG', a middleweight boxing champion who has held world titles for many years. He was born in Karaganda and has inspired thousands of young Kazakhstani people to take up boxing.

In cycling, Alexander Vinokourov won the Olympic road race in London in 2012. He has competed professionally since 1998, and his achievement remains one of the proudest moments in Kazakh sports history.

Kazakh weightlifters have also dominated international competitions. Ilya Ilyin won gold medals at two Olympic Games — Beijing in 2008 and London in 2012. He has trained since he was a young child and dedicated his life to his sport.

Today at WKU, Amir Bekzhanov dreams of continuing this tradition. He has been playing football since he was six years old. He has already represented his university in three inter-university tournaments. 'I have trained hard for four years,' he says, 'and I haven't given up yet.'

Sport teaches discipline, teamwork, and resilience. As Dr. Akhmetov always tells students: 'It doesn't matter which sport you play. What matters is that you play — because sport builds character as much as studying builds knowledge.'

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Have you seen the WKU football results? We won again!

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: That's amazing! How long have you been playing for the university team?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: For about two years now. We have played eight matches this season.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Have you ever scored in a final?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Not yet, but I haven't given up. This year feels different.
